'''Mark Braverman''' ({{Langx|he|מארק ברוורמן}}; born 1984) is an Israeli mathematician and theoretical computer scientist. He was awarded an [[EMS Prize]] in 2016 as well as [[Presburger Award]] in the same year.<ref>[http://www.7ecm.de/prizes/laureates.html 7ECM Laureates] Retrieved 2018-04-18</ref><ref>[http://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/1-news/2266-the-eatcs-bestows-the-presburger-award-2016-on-mark-braverman-princeton-university The EATCS bestows the Presburger Award 2016 on Mark Braverman] Retrieved 2018-04-18</ref> In 2019, he was awarded the [[Alan T. Waterman Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/od/waterman/waterman.jsp|title=US NSF - Office of the Director - Alan T. Waterman Award|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2019-08-10}}</ref> In 2022, he won the [[IMU Abacus Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-05 |title=Mark Braverman Wins the IMU Abacus Medal |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mark-braverman-wins-the-imu-abacus-medal-20220705/ |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref> 

He earned his doctorate from the [[University of Toronto]] in 2008, under the supervision of [[Stephen Cook]].
After this, he did post-doctoral research at [[Microsoft Research]] and then joined the faculty at University of Toronto.
In 2011, he joined the [[Princeton University]] department of computer science.<ref>[https://www.cs.princeton.edu/people/profile/mbraverm Mark Braverman | Computer Science Department at Princeton University] Retrieved 2018-04-18</ref> In 2014, he was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Interactive information and [[coding theory]]'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Seoul]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Braverman, Mark|title=Proceedings of the I International Congress of Mathematicians|chapter=Interactive information and coding theory|year=2014|pages=539–559|chapter-url=http://www.cs.princeton.edu/~mbraverm/pmwiki/uploads/ICM-2014-Braverman.pdf|archive-date=2019-01-26|access-date=2019-09-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126233725/http://www.cs.princeton.edu/~mbraverm/pmwiki/uploads/ICM-2014-Braverman.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Braverman is the son of mathematician [[Elena Braverman]]<ref>For the connection between Elena and Mark Braverman, see the dedication of Mark Braverman's master's thesis, ''Computational Complexity of Euclidean Sets: Hyperbolic Julia Sets are Poly-Time Computable'', University of Toronto, 2004.</ref> and, through her, the grandson of his co-author, mathematical statistician {{ill|Yan Petrovich Lumel'skii|ru|Лумельский, Ян Петрович}}.<ref>{{citation|last1=Braverman|first1=Mark|last2=Lumelskii|first2=Yan|doi=10.1016/S0167-7152(02)00114-1|issue=2|journal=Statistics & Probability Letters|mr=1914914|pages=157–165|title=Chebyshev systems and estimation theory for discrete distributions|volume=58|year=2002}}</ref>
